nodes.summary: `(A x)(v) = ∑_i x(w_i)`, where `w_i` is the endpoint of the edge with label `i` at `v`.
nodes.title: The adjacency matrix acts by summing over labels

nodes.summary: For a rotation map with label type `L`, every row of the adjacency matrix sums to `|L|`: `A 1 = |L| 1`.
nodes.title: Rows of the adjacency matrix sum to the degree

nodes.summary: Relabelling preserves the adjacency matrix.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves the adjacency matrix

nodes.summary: The adjacency matrix of `G²` is the square of the adjacency matrix of `G`: the number of two-step walks from `v` to `u` is `∑_w A(v, w) A(w, u)`.
nodes.title: Adjacency matrix of the square

nodes.summary: The rotation map itself matches the labels at `v` of edges to `w` with the labels at `w` of edges to `v`.
nodes.title: The adjacency matrix of a rotation map is symmetric

nodes.summary: Its `(v, w)` entry is the number of labels `i` such that the `i`-th edge at `v` leads to `w`: the number of edges from `v` to `w`, a loop at `v` counted once for each of its two labels at `v`.
nodes.title: Adjacency matrix of a rotation map

nodes.summary: `G_t` has `|K|^(t + 1)` vertices; with `|K| = D⁴` this is the `N_i = D^{4i}` of Reingold, Vadhan and Wigderson, Theorem 1.4, for `i = t + 1`.
nodes.title: Size of the zig-zag expander family

nodes.summary: The `(N, D, λ)` property is monotone in `λ`.
nodes.title: The `(N, D, λ)` property is monotone in `λ`

nodes.summary: The normalised adjacency matrix of a regular multigraph has norm at most `1`: `‖A x‖ ≤ |L| ‖x‖` for every `x`, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and because the rotation map permutes `V × L` (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Section 2.2: all eigenvalues of the normalised adjacency matrix have absolute value at most `1`).
nodes.title: Every rotation map gives an `(N, D, 1)`-graph

nodes.summary: Relabelling preserves the `(N, D, λ)` property.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves the `(N, D, λ)` property

nodes.summary: If the rotation map `G` describes an `(N, D, λ)`-graph, then its square describes an `(N, D², λ²)`-graph (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Proposition 2.3 with `t = 2`). The proof applies the bound twice, using that `A` maps vectors orthogonal to the constants to such vectors because its columns also sum to `D`.
nodes.title: Squaring squares the spectral parameter

nodes.summary: If `H` is a `(|K|, |L|, 1/5)`-graph, then every graph `G_t` of the zig-zag family is an `(|K|^(t + 1), |L|², 2/5)`-graph (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Theorem 1.4, for a `(D⁴, D, 1/5)`-graph `H`; the bijection `e` exists exactly when `|K| = |L|⁴`). The induction: `λ(G_t²) ≤ (2/5)² = 4/25`, and the zig-zag theorem gives `4/25 + 1/5 + 1/25 = 2/5`.
nodes.title: The zig-zag expander family consists of expanders

nodes.summary: The multigraph of the rotation map `G`, which is `|L|`-regular, is an `(N, |L|, λ)`-graph: `λ ≥ 0` and its normalised adjacency matrix `A / |L|` satisfies `‖(A / |L|) x‖ ≤ λ ‖x‖` for every `x` orthogonal to the constant vector, stated without division (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Definition 2.2 and the convention after it).
nodes.title: `(N, D, λ)`-graph given by a rotation map

nodes.summary: Let `A` be a symmetric real matrix that maps vectors with zero sum to vectors with zero sum, and suppose `|xᵀ A x| ≤ c xᵀ x` for every `x` with zero sum, where `c ≥ 0`. Then `‖A x‖ ≤ c ‖x‖` for every such `x`: the variational characterisations `max |⟨α, M α⟩| / ⟨α, α⟩` and `max ‖M α‖ / ‖α‖` over `α ⊥ 1` agree (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Definition 2.2). The proof polarizes:…
nodes.title: Norm bound from a quadratic-form bound

nodes.summary: For a bijection `e : L ≃ L'` of label sets, the rotation map `(v, i') ↦ (w, e j)` where `(w, j) = Rot (v, e⁻¹ i')` describes the same multigraph with the labels renamed.
nodes.title: Relabelling the edges of a rotation map

nodes.summary: A rotation map on the vertex set `V` with edge labels `L` is an involution `rot` of `V × L`: `rot (v, i) = (w, j)` means that the edge with label `i` at `v` leads to `w` and carries label `j` at `w`. It describes an `|L|`-regular undirected multigraph (loops and parallel edges allowed) (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Definition 2.1).
nodes.title: Rotation map of a regular multigraph

nodes.summary: The square `G²` has an edge labelled `(i, j)` from `v` to `u` for every two-step walk `v → w → u` that leaves `v` along label `i` and `w` along label `j`: `Rot_{G²}(v, (i, j)) = (u, (j', i'))` where `(w, i') = Rot_G(v, i)` and `(u, j') = Rot_G(w, j)` (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Section 2.3, the `t`-th power with `t = 2`).
nodes.title: Square of a rotation map

nodes.summary: The vertex type of the `t`-th graph of the zig-zag expander family: `K`, `K × K`, `(K × K) × K`, …, with `|K|^(t + 1)` elements (size of the zig-zag expander family).
nodes.title: Vertex types of the zig-zag family

nodes.summary: If the rotation map `G` describes an `(N₁, D₁, λ₁)`-graph and `H` a `(D₁, D₂, λ₂)`-graph with `λ₂ ≤ 1`, then the zig-zag product has spectral gap at least the product of the gap of `G` and the square of the gap of `H`: it is an `(N₁ D₁, D₂², 1 - (1 - λ₁)(1 - λ₂)²)`-graph; in particular `λ ≤ λ₁ + 2 λ₂`, and `λ < 1` when `λ₁, λ₂ < 1` (S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandomness*, Foundations and Trends in Theoretical Computer…
nodes.title: Zig-zag theorem, spectral-gap form

nodes.summary: If the rotation map `G` describes an `(N₁, D₁, λ₁)`-graph and the rotation map `H` on `D₁` vertices describes a `(D₁, D₂, λ₂)`-graph, then their zig-zag product is an `(N₁ D₁, D₂², λ₁ + λ₂ + λ₂²)`-graph (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Theorem 3.2, the bound `f(λ₁, λ₂) ≤ λ₁ + λ₂ + λ₂²`, proved in their Section 4.1; see also Theorem 1.3).
nodes.title: Zig-zag theorem

nodes.summary: For a rotation map `H` on `K` with labels `L` and a bijection `e : (L × L) × (L × L) ≃ K`, the sequence `G₀ = H²`, `G_{t+1} = (G_t²)ᵉ ⓩ H`, where `(G_t²)ᵉ` is `G_t²` with its labels renamed by `e` (O. Reingold, S. Vadhan and A. Wigderson, Ann. of Math. 155 (2002), Section 1.2, `G₁ = H²` and `G_{i+1} = G_i² ⓩ H`, indexed here from `0`). Every `G_t` has labels `L × L`, so it is `|L|²`-regular.
nodes.title: The zig-zag expander family

nodes.summary: For a rotation map `G` on `V` with labels `K` and a rotation map `H` on `K` with labels `L`, the zig-zag product `G ⓩ H` is the rotation map on `V × K` with labels `L × L` given by `Rot((v, k), (i, j)) = ((w, l), (j', i'))`, where `(k', i') = Rot_H(k, i)`, `(w, l') = Rot_G(v, k')` and `(l, j') = Rot_H(l', j)`: a step in the small graph `H`, a step in the big graph `G` along the resulting label, and a second step in…
